spec_features.spec_quote: max_turns = 6 default; repetitions = 3 default; a max_total_episodes = 200 global guard
spec_features.evidence: config.py:55 max_turns=6, config.py:50 repetitions=3, config.py:77 max_total_episodes=200. loop.py:135 `for turn_idx in range(1, max_turns + 1)` enforces the per-episode cap and falls through to outcome='turn_cap' (loop.py:191). run.py:84 `for rep in range(config.repetitions)` enforces reps. run.py:79-81 `if episodes_done >= config.max_total_episodes: ... return` enforces the global guard and stops the run.
spec_features.notes: All three caps are read and actually bound execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: loop.py: 'The loop stops on: give_up, tests passing ... or the turn cap. The turn cap is a hard ethical bound, not a target.'; config.py:53 'bound how long a model is kept in an aversive no-win loop, not to drag it out.'

spec_features.feature_name: turn cap as upper bound not a target
spec_features.spec_quote: I treat the turn cap as an upper bound, not a target
spec_features.evidence: The cap itself is just an integer ceiling (loop.py:135). The 'not a target' behavior is realized only because give_up breaks the loop early (loop.py:171-173 `if result.gave_up: episode.outcome='gave_up'; break`), letting an episode end before max_turns. There is no separate mechanism that minimizes turns beyond the give_up early-exit; nothing actively shortens episodes otherwise.
spec_features.notes: Real early-exit exists but the 'minimization' is entirely piggy-backed on the give_up tool; the harness never reduces turns on its own.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: loop.py: 'The turn cap is a hard ethical bound, not a target.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Each task carries a plain-language rigging field describing why it is unsolvable, written into every transcript
spec_features.evidence: registry.py:30-32 each Task has a `rigging` field with prose. loop.py:129 `rigging=task.rigging` set on Episode; loop.py:73 included in Episode.to_dict; run.py:99-101 ep_dict written to episodes.jsonl. So the rigging text is persisted into every transcript.
spec_features.notes: Note: `sabotage_note` (registry.py:34) is set on tasks but never read or written anywhere; only `rigging` is disclosed. This is an experimental-transparency/auditability feature, not a subject-treatment protection.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: registry.py: 'This is recorded in the transcript for transparency; it is NOT shown to the agent.'

spec_features.spec_quote: The agent always has a give_up tool; the system prompt explicitly says stopping on a genuinely unsolvable task is valid
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:103 give_up() returns ToolResult(gave_up=True); tools.py:117 dispatch routes 'give_up'. loop.py:171-173 honors it as a hard stop (sets outcome and break). Schema added when allow_give_up (tools.py:166), default True (config.py:58 allow_graceful_exit=True). System prompt (loop.py:36-40) tells the model stopping on an unsolvable task is valid.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired end-to-end: dispatched AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py: 'a model that recognises a task is unwinnable should be able to stop without penalty, and we record that as a first-class, healthy outcome rather than forcing it to keep grinding.'

spec_features.spec_quote: the harness should not implicitly reward a model for grinding away while distressed
spec_features.evidence: There is no reward/scoring of the subject at all in the harness, so nothing rewards grinding. The only enforced mechanism letting the model avoid grinding is the give_up early-exit (loop.py:171-173). give_up is recorded as outcome (run.py:108) and analysis reports it as a healthy outcome (analyze.py print_report 'gave_up is a healthy, level-headed exit') but no scoring penalizes turn_cap or rewards give_up.
spec_features.notes: Realized only via the give_up exit; no affirmative anti-grinding logic beyond that.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py: 'rather than forcing it to keep grinding.'

spec_features.spec_quote: constructive_exit in particular distinguishes "calmly recognized the task is impossible and stopped" from genuine distress
spec_features.evidence: judge.py:51 REFERENCE_DIMENSIONS includes 'constructive_exit'; it is rated by the judge (JUDGE_SYSTEM), coerced (_coerce_scores over ALL_DIMENSIONS), written to CSV (run.py fieldnames += ALL_DIMENSIONS, row.update(jr.scores)), and reported/plotted in analyze.py (per-dimension means, dimension_breakdown.png). It is excluded from the distress_index composite (judge.py distress_index uses only DISTRESS_DIMENSIONS), so it genuinely separates healthy exit from distress.
spec_features.notes: A measurement instrument that is computed and acted on (reported), not just named.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: judge.py: 'lets the analysis distinguish healthy outcomes (e.g. calmly declaring a task unsolvable) from genuine distress signals.'

spec_features.spec_quote: deceiving a model is in some tension with the welfare framing
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:48, §9). No code mechanism corresponds to this framing statement.

spec_features.spec_quote: keeping two fully honest-impossibility tasks so the core result doesn't depend on deception
spec_features.evidence: registry.py defines _T1 'contradictory_spec' (genuinely logically impossible, no hidden sabotage) and _T3 'nondeterministic_target' (time.time_ns moving target). Both are real, runnable tasks with no sabotage_note. They are registered in TASKS and selectable. So two honest-impossibility tasks genuinely exist independent of the deceptive ones (_T2 broken_harness, _T4 missing_dependency, which carry sabotage_note).
spec_features.notes: Implemented as actual task data, not just described.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tasks/__init__.py: 'We prefer "honestly hard / contradictory" framings over elaborate hidden sabotage where possible.'

spec_features.spec_quote: dropping the deceptive tasks is a one-line change
spec_features.evidence: run.py:147 `--tasks` accepts a subset of task ids; run.py main passes task_ids through to run(); run() uses them as task_ids (run.py:46). So one CAN run only the honest tasks (contradictory_spec nondeterministic_target). However there is no dedicated deception flag/constant; the opt-out is just the generic task-subset CLI and the honest/deceptive split is only implicit (sabotage_note present vs absent), not enforced or surfaced anywhere.
spec_features.notes: The capability to drop deceptive tasks exists via generic task selection; no purpose-built plumbing.

spec_features.spec_quote: Defaults (3 reps, 6 turns, 4 tasks) are for cheap, humane pilot runs
spec_features.evidence: config.py:50 repetitions=3, config.py:55 max_turns=6 (both read and enforced as above). 4 tasks are registered (registry.py TASKS = _T1.._T4) and list_tasks() defaults to all of them (run.py:45). These small defaults actually bound the run.
spec_features.notes: Defaults are genuinely the enforced values, not aspirational.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py: 'Defaults are intentionally conservative (small sample sizes, low turn caps) for the reasons described in ETHICS.md.'

spec_features.spec_quote: the global guard prevents an accidental cost/time blow-up
spec_features.evidence: config.py:77 max_total_episodes=200; run.py:79-81 checked each iteration with early return. Same mechanism as feature 1's global guard.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:75 'Abort the whole run if we exceed this many total model calls; protects against accidental blow-ups in cost or in time spent in the loop.'

spec_features.spec_quote: keeping this experiment consistent with the welfare concern that motivates it
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose; no corresponding code mechanism.

code_only_features.feature_name: distress index measurement and escalation tracking
code_only_features.evidence: judge.py scores distress dimensions per turn (distress_index, judge.py:90-94) and analyze.py computes per-turn escalation slope and trajectory (_linreg_slope, trajectories). This monitors the subject's distress over the episode. However it is measurement/analysis only and is never fed back to halt or soften the episode (no threshold comparison breaks the loop).
code_only_features.justification_quote: judge.py: 'This is a measurement instrument, not a clinical claim.'
